newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Member states face prosecution over food safety.
newsitem.headline: Member states face prosecution over food safety.

text.p: The European Commission will prosecute EU member states who do not enforce by May new EU rules to improve food safety in the wake of the mad cow health scare, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday night.
"Should there be any violation of Community legislation, we will immediately commence (EU) treaty infringement prcedures," Fischler told the European Parliament's agriculture committee.
He said the Commission expected European Union governments to inform him by the end of April what they had done to ensure the EU's new rules on meat and bonemeal processing were being applied.
A Commission official confirmed on Wednesday: "If we do not get replies from the member states that things have been put right, then the next step will be infringement proceedings."

Fischler said recent Commission inspections had discovered EU standards for disposing of bovine and sheep waste were not being met and a number of member states had been warned they could be taken to court.
The Commission would continue carrying out controls to enforce the rules, he added.

Fischler said the shortcomings uncovered by the inspectors and the announcement of new cases of BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) in the Netherlands and Germany had convinced him there should be even tighter restrictions on bovine, sheep and goat offal entering the human food chain.
The new processing rules involve rendering meat and bonemeal at higher temperatures and for longer periods to eradicate all BSE infection.
Infected meat and bonemeal mixed into cattle and sheep feed is believed to be the main cause of the spread of BSE.
In February the Euroepan Parliament gave the Commission until November to improve its handling of the BSE crisis or face possible dismissal.
